article.headline: Serenity Maps the Next Rotation in AI Infrastructure Investing
article.lede: A chart circulating in AI-investment circles distils analyst Serenity's view of where the asymmetric opportunities in the AI hardware build-out lie — and which bets are already too crowded to bother with. Serenity, the X handle of a supply-chain analyst who built a following of roughly 130,000 by front-running institutional capital into semiconductor chokepoints, has sequenced four investment horizons from 'the edge is already gone' to 'the edge hasn't formed yet.' The poster, @LIWEI_TWCapital, amplifies the framework without commentary; the substance is Serenity's.
article.body:
Serenity (@aleabitoreddit), known on Reddit's r/WallStreetBets as u/AleaBito, describes himself as an AI and semiconductor supply-chain analyst and former AI research scientist. His core framework — which he calls *AI Supply Chain Structural Bottleneck* analysis — involves reverse-engineering production chains to find the single irreplaceable node that cannot scale as fast as demand. Rather than buying obvious beneficiaries, he hunts for what he terms "functional monopolies": critical inputs trading at compressed valuations before fund managers discover them. His most-cited call was AXT Inc. (AXTI), an indium-phosphide substrate maker he identified at $12; the stock eventually reached $70 and the thesis earned him a ban from r/WallStreetBets.

**HBM** — *High Bandwidth Memory* — anchors the chart's 'present, boom ending' zone. HBM is DRAM stacked vertically using *through-silicon vias* (TSVs) and bonded directly to a GPU interposer, delivering four to eight times the bandwidth of standard DRAM at lower power. Every NVIDIA (NVDA) AI accelerator ships with it, making the three producers — SK Hynix (000660.KS), Samsung Electronics (005930.KS), and Micron Technology (MU) — the most supply-constrained nodes in the 2024 AI build-out. SK Hynix reported a 405 percent year-over-year operating-profit increase in Q1 2026, with HBM supply sold out through year-end. Serenity's call is not that HBM demand is collapsing; it is that the asymmetric investor edge has already been captured. New fab capacity from SK Hynix's M15X facility (mid-2027) and Samsung's Pyeongtaek expansion threaten the oversupply that has historically ended semiconductor supercycles.

Optical communication occupies the same 'boom ending' bucket — the category Serenity credits as his most profitable thesis of 2024 and 2025. As AI clusters scale from thousands to millions of GPUs, copper interconnects become prohibitively power-hungry. Pluggable optical transceivers solved the immediate bottleneck; *co-packaged optics* (CPO), where the photonic die is integrated directly alongside the switching chip, is the next generation. In March 2026, NVIDIA committed $4 billion split between Coherent Corp. (COHR) and Lumentum Holdings (LITE) to secure priority CPO production capacity. Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI) reported Q1 2026 revenue up 51 percent year-over-year as data-center shipments more than doubled. Serenity's earlier substrate plays — AXTI for indium phosphide, Soitec (SOI.PA) for *silicon-on-insulator* (SOI) wafers — reflect his preference for raw-material chokepoints that are less visible to generalist investors. His current focus has migrated further down the stack toward *external light sources* (ELS) and companies such as Sivers Semiconductors (SIVE.ST), a sub-$300 million-market-cap ELS laser maker.

Space exploration and infrastructure occupies the five-to-ten-year 'long-term opportunity' band. The connection to AI is not primarily about satellite imagery: it is about **power arbitrage**. Terrestrial data-center buildout is constrained by power-grid capacity — gas turbine backlogs currently run roughly seven years — while orbit offers uninterrupted solar exposure at roughly eight times the ground-level flux. NVIDIA in 2026 launched its Space-1 Vera Rubin module for orbital compute, claiming 25 times the AI throughput of an H100, with early partners including Planet Labs (PL) and Starcloud. Starcloud raised $170 million in a March 2026 Series A to put GPU clusters in orbit, but current orbital rack costs sit around $3.5 million per month — orders of magnitude above ground-based colocation. The five-to-ten-year horizon reflects the cost curves that must close before the economics make commercial sense.

Humanoid robots sit at the furthest horizon: future growth over five to ten years. Tesla (TSLA) had deployed more than 1,000 Optimus Gen 3 units inside its Gigafactories by early 2026, but CEO Elon Musk acknowledged on the Q4 2025 earnings call that they were "not doing useful work" yet. Figure AI, backed by NVIDIA and valued at $39 billion after its Series C, generated its first commercial revenue only in January 2025. Goldman Sachs projects 1.4 million humanoid shipments industry-wide by 2035. The gap between convincing demonstrations and reliable autonomous performance in unstructured environments remains the central engineering problem, and Serenity's 5-10-year framing aligns with where most professional forecasts cluster.

concepts.definition: A type of DRAM in which multiple chips are stacked vertically and connected by through-silicon vias, then bonded directly to a GPU interposer. The result is four to eight times the memory bandwidth of conventional DRAM at lower power — essential for AI accelerators that must shuttle enormous datasets between compute and memory.

A vertical electrical channel drilled through a silicon chip, allowing stacked dies to communicate without external wiring. TSVs are the enabling manufacturing technology for HBM and advanced 3D chip packaging more broadly.

An interconnect approach in which photonic components — lasers and modulators that transmit data as pulses of light — are integrated into the same package as the network switch chip, rather than connected via pluggable external transceivers. CPO cuts power consumption dramatically and is widely seen as mandatory for next-generation AI cluster interconnects at terabit-scale.

In a co-packaged optics system, the laser that generates the optical signal is sometimes kept physically separate from the switch package and fed in via fiber. This preserves thermal isolation and makes the laser replaceable independently of the switch. Companies specialising in ELS components — such as Sivers Semiconductors — occupy a narrow chokepoint in the CPO supply chain.

A wafer technology in which a thin crystalline silicon layer sits atop an insulating layer of silicon dioxide. SOI reduces parasitic capacitance and electrical leakage, making it well suited for the high-speed photonic chips used in optical interconnects. Soitec holds a dominant position in SOI wafer production.

Serenity's investment framework: rather than buying the dominant final product (e.g., NVIDIA GPUs), identify the single most concentrated, irreplaceable upstream input whose capacity cannot grow as fast as end demand. The thesis is that these chokepoints trade at depressed valuations before institutions discover them, producing asymmetric risk-reward for early movers.

Serenity's term for a supplier that is the only practical source of a critical input within the relevant time horizon — not legally protected, but effectively uncontestable because of technical complexity, long capital cycles, or customer qualification barriers. The investment thesis requires that the monopoly position is real and durable enough to extract pricing power as demand surges.

The sequential movement of large professional investors from one sector or theme to another as prior trades become crowded. Serenity's framework assumes that investors who identify each rotation early can buy ahead of the institutional wave and exit into the liquidity that large fund inflows provide.

The economic argument for placing compute infrastructure in Earth orbit: satellites receive uninterrupted solar power at roughly eight times the flux available at the ground, potentially allowing AI data centres to bypass terrestrial grid constraints and multi-year interconnection queues. The arbitrage is real in principle but requires orbital rack costs to fall by orders of magnitude before it becomes commercially competitive.

A compound semiconductor with properties that make it superior to silicon for high-speed and photonic applications. InP substrates are the raw material for the laser diodes and photodetectors at the heart of optical transceivers, making substrate producers a foundational chokepoint in the photonics supply chain.

article.fact_check: The chart's sequencing is broadly defensible, but two points deserve scrutiny. First, labelling HBM 'boom ending' overstates the fundamental demand picture: SK Hynix's HBM allocation is sold out through end-2026 and the company has described customer reservations extending three years forward. The 'ending' applies to the investor edge — institutions are now crowded in — not to the underlying shortage, which persists until new fab capacity arrives in 2027-2028. Second, Serenity's portfolio-return figures (variously cited on his own feed as +316% to +501% to +1,116% year-to-date at different moments) are entirely self-reported and unaudited. Individual directional calls have been documented, but aggregate performance numbers should be treated as illustrative rather than verified fact.

ticker_axti.name: AXT, Inc.
ticker_axti.blurb: AXT, Inc. designs, develops, manufactures, and distributes compound and single-element semiconductor substrates used across a wide range of high-growth applications. Its core product is indium phosphide (InP), which is critical for data center optical interconnects, silicon photonics, photonic integrated circuits, 5G communications, fiber optic lasers and detectors, and lidar systems for robotics and autonomous vehicles. Founded in 1986 and publicly listed since May 1998, AXT employs approximately 1,541 people and sits within the Semiconductor Equipment & Materials segment of the technology sector. The company is positioned as a key upstream supplier in the AI-driven buildout of high-speed optical data infrastructure.
ticker_axti.recent: AXT reported stellar Q1 2026 earnings on April 30, 2026, triggering a surge to an all-time high of $134.00 — an extraordinary move given its 52-week low of $1.38, representing roughly a 100x run in under a year. The stock pulled back roughly 12–13% in the days following the high before rebounding ~21% in the subsequent week, with shares around $121–122 as of May 13, 2026. Despite a market cap now exceeding $7.5B on trailing revenue of only ~$95.9M and a negative net income of ~$14.3M, the market is pricing in aggressive future growth, reflected in a forward P/E near 265; consensus analyst price targets (~$57) lag far behind current trading levels.

ticker_nvda.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ticker_nvda.blurb: NVIDIA designs graphics processing units (GPUs) and system-on-chip products. Originally a gaming chip company, it became the dominant supplier of AI accelerators — chips that perform the parallel matrix math required to train and run large language models. Its H100, H200, and Blackwell GPU families are the de facto standard for AI training infrastructure at hyperscalers and cloud providers. NVIDIA's CUDA software ecosystem creates deep switching costs: virtually all AI frameworks and models are optimised for CUDA, making competing hardware difficult to adopt at scale. NVIDIA also sells networking (InfiniBand, Ethernet) and data-centre systems.
ticker_nvda.recent: NVIDIA reported FY2026 (ending Jan 2026) revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65% YoY, with data centre revenue reaching $186 billion. The company's forward P/E of ~17.5x on 34.8% projected EPS growth produces a PEG of 0.50 — unusually cheap for what is arguably the most critical infrastructure company in the AI buildout. Hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta) collectively committed over $200 billion in AI infrastructure capex for 2026, the majority flowing through NVIDIA's supply chain.

It is one of the world's largest memory chipmakers, competing directly with Samsung Electronics and Micron Technology.

The stock hit a 52-week high of 1,653,000 KRW, reflecting strong demand for AI-related memory chips. Morningstar raised its fair value estimate by 65% following the earnings report.

ticker_005930-ks.blurb: Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. is a South Korean multinational electronics company and the world's largest manufacturer of memory chips, smartphones, and consumer electronics. As of 2026, it holds a dominant market position in memory and mobile devices, with a market cap exceeding 1,700 trillion KRW.

ticker_mu.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
ticker_mu.blurb: Micron is the only US-headquartered manufacturer of DRAM and NAND memory at scale, competing with Samsung and SK Hynix. Historically the most cyclical of the three, it has spent the past two years repositioning toward high-bandwidth memory (HBM), the stacked DRAM that pairs with AI accelerators, where pricing is multiples of standard DDR5 and contracts are multi-year rather than spot.
ticker_mu.recent: In March 2026 Micron began mass production of HBM4 12-Hi 36GB stacks for Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform; management has stated 2026 HBM capacity is sold out under binding agreements. Fiscal Q2 2026 revenue was around $23.9 billion, with non-GAAP gross margin near 75%. The board approved a 30% dividend increase and roughly $25 billion of fiscal-2026 capex. Despite a strong year-to-date move, the forward P/E remains in the high single digits on consensus, reflecting residual cyclicality scepticism.

ticker_cohr.name: Coherent Corp.
ticker_cohr.blurb: Coherent Corp. (formerly II-VI Incorporated, rebranded after the 2022 acquisition of Lumentum rival Coherent) develops and manufactures engineered materials, optoelectronic components, and laser systems across three segments: Networking, Materials, and Lasers. Its Networking segment — the primary AI data-center play — supplies indium-phosphide chips, transceiver modules, and silicon-photonics sub-assemblies to hyperscalers and networking OEMs. With roughly $5.8 billion in fiscal 2025 revenue, it is one of the largest vertically integrated photonics companies in the world.
ticker_cohr.recent: Coherent joined the S&P 500 in March 2026, the same month it announced general availability of the industry's first dual-laser QSFP28-DCO module — a compact form factor enabling 100G coherent transmission over a single fiber with up to 300 km reach. At OFC 2026 the company showcased an expanded InP portfolio including 400 mW CW lasers, 200G/400G photodiodes, and 800G/1.6T modulators. Fifteen analysts hold an average "Strong Buy" rating with a consensus 12-month price target near $278.

ticker_lite.name: Lumentum Holdings Inc.
ticker_lite.blurb: Lumentum makes the lasers, optical chips, and components that go into the high-speed transceivers wiring AI data centres together. Spun out of JDSU in 2015, it spent its first decade as a 3D-sensing and telecom-optics supplier of moderate growth. The AI-cluster build-out has remade it into one of the principal upstream beneficiaries of hyperscaler capex, alongside Coherent Corp.
ticker_lite.recent: Q1 fiscal-2026 set record revenue, with management citing AI-driven demand and an order book that runs into 2027. In March 2026 Nvidia announced a roughly $2 billion strategic investment paired with multi-year purchase commitments for co-packaged-optics components. The company joined the S&P 500 in March 2026; shares have surged on AI demand, leaving the stock at a forward P/E in the 60s, materially above peers.

ticker_aaoi.name: Applied Optoelectronics, Inc.
ticker_aaoi.blurb: Applied Optoelectronics is a Texas-based maker of optical components and transceivers, historically known for serving cable-television networks and a handful of hyperscale customers in cycles of feast and famine. The AI build-out has dragged it firmly into the data-centre supply chain, where it now competes for 400G, 800G, and 1.6T transceiver volumes against Lumentum, Coherent, Innolight, and Eoptolink.
ticker_aaoi.recent: Management is guiding to full-year 2026 revenue exceeding $1 billion, more than double 2025's roughly $456 million, on the back of 800G ramps and a single 1.6T order disclosed at over $200 million. The company aims to scale from roughly 90,000 800G units per month at end-2025 toward 500,000 800G/1.6T units per month by end-2026. The stock hit an all-time high near $192 in early May 2026, having traded as low as $12.56 within the last 52 weeks.

ticker_soi-pa.name: Soitec SA
ticker_soi-pa.blurb: Soitec SA is a French semiconductor materials company founded in 1992 that develops and manufactures engineered substrates used in smartphones, automotive electronics, and 5G infrastructure. Its core product lines include Radio Frequency Silicon-on-Insulator (RF-SOI) wafers for smartphone front-end modules, FD-SOI substrates for low-power chips, Piezoelectric-on-Insulator (POI) RF filters, and RF gallium nitride for sub-6GHz and mmWave 5G systems. The company operates across Asia, Europe, and the United States with approximately 1,991 employees and a market capitalization of roughly €5.6 billion. Soitec holds a dominant position in the engineered substrate niche, supplying major semiconductor fabs and OEMs globally.
ticker_soi-pa.recent: As of mid-May 2026, Soitec shares trade around €152–155, well off their 52-week high of €180 but up sharply over the prior year (+163%) following a reverse stock split. Trailing-twelve-month revenue has contracted 14.3% to €784M and net income has fallen nearly 90% year-over-year, reflecting weakness in smartphone demand — a risk Morningstar analysts flagged in a March 2026 note that also cited silicon photonics as a potential long-term upside catalyst. The company's next scheduled earnings release is May 27, 2026, which will be closely watched for signs of stabilization in mobile volumes.

ticker_pl.name: Planet Labs PBC
ticker_pl.blurb: Planet Labs PBC designs, builds, and operates the world's largest commercial Earth-observation satellite constellation, anchored by its SuperDove fleet of small satellites that image the entire planet daily at up to 3.5-meter ground sampling distance. The company delivers this high-cadence geospatial data to government, agriculture, forestry, infrastructure, and financial-intelligence customers through a cloud-based subscription platform. Founded in 2010 and headquartered in San Francisco, Planet went public via SPAC in December 2021 and employs roughly 1,000 people. Despite strong revenue growth—trailing-twelve-month revenue of ~$308M, up ~26% year-over-year—the company remains unprofitable, posting a net loss of ~$247M (EPS –$0.80).
ticker_pl.recent: PL shares closed at $40.74 on May 13, 2026, just below their 52-week high of $43.12 and far above the 52-week low of $3.47, reflecting a staggering ~1,268% appreciation in market capitalization over the past year. The rally appears driven by renewed investor appetite for commercial space and geospatial-intelligence assets, though specific catalysts within the past 30 days are not detailed in available sources. The company's next earnings report is scheduled for June 4, 2026, and analyst consensus price targets (~$27.64) trail the current price significantly, suggesting the market is pricing in substantial forward growth expectations.

ticker_tsla.name: Tesla Inc.
ticker_tsla.blurb: Tesla designs and manufactures battery-electric vehicles, energy storage systems, and solar products. Founded in 2003 and taken public in June 2010 at seventeen dollars per share, it became one of the most spectacular long-term equity stories of the 2010s: every share from the IPO, adjusted for subsequent stock splits, would be worth roughly 6,500 dollars by late 2025 — a return of approximately 22,000 percent. The company's Model S (2012), Model 3 (2017), and Model Y (2020) progressively expanded the addressable market from luxury to mass-market segments. Tesla also operates a global Supercharger network and a large-scale energy storage division (Megapack). CEO Elon Musk's public profile — across social media, SpaceX, and his acquisition of X (formerly Twitter) — has made Tesla one of the more volatile large-cap equities in recent years, as investor sentiment toward the company has become partially indexed to sentiment toward Musk personally.
ticker_tsla.recent: Tesla has faced intensifying competition from Chinese electric-vehicle manufacturers, particularly BYD, which overtook Tesla in global EV sales in 2023. Revenue growth decelerated sharply in 2024, and the company has relied on price cuts to defend market share, compressing margins. Musk's political visibility during the 2024 US election cycle and his role in the DOGE cost-cutting initiative generated significant consumer backlash in some markets, with Tesla registrations declining in Europe and California in early 2025. The stock traded in a wide range through 2025-2026 as investors weighed the autonomous-vehicle (Full Self-Driving) optionality against near-term margin pressure.
